fixes.explanation: The text doesn't mention the fire going out. Peter goes out to the gateway, and then the rooster crowed. Fire's not the answer here, friend.

The text doesn't mention a city wall. It says Peter follows at a distance, right into the courtyard of the high priest. Peter, one of Jesus' followers, goes all the way in. I think I'd have been the one at the edge holding up a sign saying 'Good luck!'

Peter, one of Jesus' followers, doesn't stop partway. The text says he follows right into the high priest's courtyard. He stays back at a distance, but he keeps coming all the way in. The text doesn't mention the Kidron Valley.
Hides is a fair guess, but that's not the word the text uses. Peter sits with the officers and warms himself by the fire. Warming is what he's doing there.

Not quite, friend. The text says many bore false witness against Jesus, but their testimony was inconsistent. The chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were seeking testimony to put Him to death, but they did not find any. Stories that don't match each other don't give them what they're looking for.
False is right. Many bore false witness against Jesus, but their testimony was inconsistent. Their stories don't line up. That's many witnesses, and still they did not find any testimony.

That's the claim. Some men stand up and testify falsely against Him: “We heard Him say, ‘I will destroy this man-made temple, and in three days I will build another that is made without hands.’” Then the text adds, “But even their testimony was inconsistent.” So this is what they say, and even it doesn't hold together.
No seven years in this one, friend. The men claim Jesus said He would destroy this man-made temple and in three days build another made without hands. Three days, not seven years.
The text doesn't show Jesus calling any witnesses. It says He remained silent and made no reply. The witnesses we hear about are the ones testifying against Him, and their testimony was inconsistent.
True. Asked, “Are You the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?” Jesus says, “I am.” After all that silence, it's a short, plain answer.
He tears them. The high priest tears his clothes and declares, “Why do we need any more witnesses?” That's a big move in front of the whole council.
The text says the high priest tore his clothes. Taking them off isn't what it says. It happens at this moment, right after Jesus answers.
Ignoring isn't what the text says. It says Peter denied it again. Denying means saying no, and that's what he does.

He breaks down and weeps. Peter remembers the word Jesus had spoken to him: “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.” I think that's a man whose heart just broke. A sad moment, and an honest one.
